summary: CheerPlanner v92 Household Privacy Controls — FULL PASS. Backend 8/8 pytest tests passed; frontend UI end-to-end verified against a real coparent joined via invite code. Owner sees per-member 'Expenses & payments' + 'Travel & bookings' toggles (correct testIDs), toggle persists across reload, DB reflects state, and the blocked coparent experience is complete: Expenses bottom tab hidden, dashboard finance tiles (This month / Paid YTD / Raised / Expenses due) not rendered, GET /api/expenses returns 403; with travel OFF the competition detail hides the 'Travel & accommodations' section and GET /api/bookings returns 403. Owner is never blocked (all tabs + finance visible). PATCH permissions verified: non-owner → 403, self-block → 400. /auth/me exposes visibility{expenses,travel}, /api/household returns is_owner + members[].privacy + owner_user_id, /api/dashboard returns can_view_expenses/can_view_travel and zeroes hidden areas. No regressions detected.
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend caches /auth/me visibility in AuthContext at login/bootstrap; a blocked member won't see UI update until the next app focus or relogin. Main agent already flagged this as acceptable for MVP. If desired later, refresh visibility on window focus.
household.tsx togglePrivacy optimistically updates local state before PATCH — correctly reverts via load() on error (nice).
seed_data_creation: Created a throwaway coparent test user (testcoparent_<hex>@example.com) via /api/auth/signup, joined the owner's household through a fresh invite code, exercised the toggles, then removed them via /api/household/leave. No lingering test data in the owner's household.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Household privacy feature (v92) is fully validated. If iterating further, the pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_iter92_household_privacy.py is a good regression baseline. Frontend uses testIDs privacy-expenses-<memberId> and privacy-travel-<memberId>. Owner: applereview@cheerplanner.app / Review2026!.
